topicTitle: Effect — typed functional effects in TypeScript
courseLine: Official Effect docs · fibers, Schema, Context/Layers, resource safety, and schedules

prompts.title: Install Effect, strict TypeScript, and your first runnable program
prompts.query: I am setting up Effect in a new TypeScript project. Walk through prerequisites (TypeScript version, strict tsconfig), installing the `effect` package, choosing a runner (tsx / node / bun), and a minimal program using `Console.log` and `Effect.runSync` or `Effect.runPromise`. Explain what “lazy” means for Effect values and one common mistake (accidentally running side effects at module load time).

prompts.title: The Effect type: success, errors, and requirements (R channel)
prompts.query: Teach `Effect<A, E, R>` in plain language: what each type parameter means, how requirements accumulate when composing effects, and how `never` is used for “no error” or “no requirements.” Compare briefly to Promise typing. Show how to extract inferred types with `Effect.Success`, `Effect.Error`, and `Effect.Context`, and when to prefer `runPromiseExit` over `runPromise` for inspection.

prompts.title: `Effect.gen` and `yield*`: readable control flow without async/await
prompts.query: Explain how to structure programs with `Effect.gen` and generator functions: `yield*` vs returning plain values, short-circuiting on failure, using normal `if`/`for`/`while` inside generators, and how this differs from `async`/`await` in terms of interruption and typed errors. Include a small example that sequences a few effects and fails early.

prompts.title: Expected failures vs defects, plus `catchTag` / `catchTags` patterns
prompts.query: Contrast expected (typed) errors vs unexpected defects in Effect. Show practical patterns: `Effect.fail`, `Data.TaggedError` / yieldable errors, `Effect.catchTag` and `Effect.catchTags`, and when `catchAllDefect` or similar tools matter. Give guidance on modeling domain errors so they remain recoverable and observable.

prompts.title: Effect Schema: decoding unknown inputs and round-tripping encodings
prompts.query: Introduce `effect/Schema` for validating external data: `Schema` type parameters (Type, Encoded, Requirements), decoding from `unknown`, encoding back out, and why round-trip consistency matters. Mention optional `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` interactions and when to prefer `decodeUnknownSync` vs async decode paths for IO boundaries.

prompts.title: Context tags and `provideService`: dependency injection without globals
prompts.query: Explain services in Effect using `Context.Tag` (class Tag pattern), accessing implementations with `yield* MyService`, and providing implementations via `Effect.provideService`. Contrast interface design that leaks dependencies vs keeping service methods returning plain `Effect` values without extra requirements in their signatures.

prompts.title: Layers: composing constructors for services and their dependencies
prompts.query: Teach `Layer` as a blueprint for building services: `Layer.succeed`, `Layer.effect`, merging layers, and `Effect.provide(program, layer)` to eliminate requirements. Use a small dependency graph (for example Config → Logger → Database) to show how layers avoid leaking transitive dependencies into public service interfaces.

prompts.title: Resource safety: `Effect.scoped`, finalizers, and release on interruption
prompts.query: Describe how Effect ensures cleanup: `Effect.ensuring` / `Effect.onExit`, scoped resources, `Effect.addFinalizer`, and why finalizer order is reversed. Give a concrete pattern for “acquire → use → always release” that still works when the workflow fails or is interrupted mid-flight.

prompts.title: Concurrency: `Effect.all` options, fibers, fork/join, and interruption
prompts.query: Cover Effect concurrency basics: default sequential `Effect.all`, `concurrency` options, `Effect.fork` / joining fibers, and cooperative interruption (`Fiber.interrupt`, `Effect.interrupt`). Explain supervision at a high level (child fibers tied to parent scope) and when to reach for higher-level combinators instead of manual fiber juggling.

prompts.title: Streams: multiple emissions, backpressure intuition, and `Stream` vs `Effect`
prompts.query: Explain `Stream<A, E, R>` as an extension of `Effect` that can emit many values: finite vs infinite streams, common constructors (`Stream.fromIterable`, `Stream.range`, `Stream.async`), and typical use cases (event batches, pagination, replacing ad-hoc async iterators). Mention how errors and requirements line up with the stream type.

prompts.title: Schedules: retries, backoff, repetition, and composing policies
prompts.query: Introduce `Schedule<Out, In, R>`: how schedules consume inputs (errors for retry, values for repeat), composing schedules (`union`, `intersect`), and wiring schedules into `Effect.retry` / repetition workflows. Give practical recipes for exponential backoff with caps and jitter at a conceptual level.

prompts.title: Testing: `TestClock`, `TestContext`, and swapping layers for fakes
prompts.query: Outline a testing strategy for Effect programs: controlling time with `TestClock.adjust`, using `Effect.provide` / test layers to replace real IO with fakes, and keeping tests deterministic. Mention `Effect.runPromiseExit` in tests for asserting failures without thrown rejections, and one pitfall (forgetting to fork before advancing time when sleep is involved).
